activity_context.topic_title: Expressing Rational Functions with Irreducible Quadratic Factors as Sums of Partial Fractions

feedback.problem: Express $\frac{4{x}^{2}+10x+6}{({x}^{2}+3x+4)(x+3)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
feedback.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4{x}^{2}+10x+6}{({x}^{2}+3x+4)(x+3)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+3x+4)}+\frac{C}{(x+3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+3x+4$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $\frac{4{x}^{2}+10x+6}{({x}^{2}+3x+4)(x+3)}$ and get

$$
4{x}^{2}+10x+6=(Ax+B)(x+3)+C({x}^{2}+3x+4).
$$

Plugging in $x=-3$ eliminates the $A$ and $B$ terms and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4(-3)^{2}+10(-3)+6 & =(A(-3)+B)(-3+3)+C((-3)^{2}+3(-3)+4) \\ 36-30+6 & =4C \\ 12 & =4C \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2}+10(0)+6 & =(A(0)+B)(0+3)+C({0}^{2}+3(0)+4) \\ 6 & =3B+4C \\ 6 & =3B+4(3) \\ 3B & =6-12 \\ B & =\frac{-6}{3} \\ B & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=1$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}4(1)^{2}+10(1)+6 & =(A(1)+B)(1+3)+C({1}^{2}+3(1)+4) \\ 20 & =4A+4B+8C \\ 20 & =4A+4(-2)+8(3) \\ 4A & =20+8-24 \\ A & =\frac{4}{4} \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=1,B=-2,$ and $C=3.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}+10x+6}{({x}^{2}+3x+4)(x+3)}=\frac{x-2}{({x}^{2}+3x+4)}+\frac{3}{(x+3)}.
$$
